steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: INPUT: gets data from the user (or another source) and stores it in a variable. In most pseudo-code, INPUT returns a string, so you may need to convert it to the correct data type. | Important: Data received via INPUT is usually a string. If you need to perform arithmetic, you must convert it using INT(), FLOAT(), or other type conversion functions. | OUTPUT: displays data to the user. You can output variables, strings, numbers, and expressions. Use & to concatenate (join) items in the output. | String operations: allow you to manipulate text data. At GCSE, you need to know LENGTH, POSITION (or INSTR), SUBSTRING, and concatenation.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: What does LENGTH("GCSE Computer Science") return? | Write pseudo-code that asks for a word and outputs the first three characters. | What is the ASCII code for 'A'? What is CHR(97)?
